segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hello and welcome to Real Easy English. In this podcast, we have real conversations in easy English to help you learn.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm Neil.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And I'm Georgie. Remember, you can watch a video version of this podcast on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: How are you today, Georgie?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I'm very well, thank you, today. Neil, how are you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm OK. I've got one or two little worries.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Have you? Well, that's interesting because we are talking about worries today in this podcast.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Worries are problems that make you feel upset or scared. So, shall we start the conversation?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Let's do it.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So, Neil, you said you've got a couple of little worries. Do you want to share them?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah. I think when you have kids, you're kind of slightly worried all the time.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And yesterday my son got hurt playing cricket. And so this morning I just wanted to make

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: sure he was feeling okay before he went to school.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And how was he this morning?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: He seemed okay.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah Seemed a bit bruised

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Oh no An injury to the knee or something

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Shoulder

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Ouch

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And arm

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Gosh

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And are you someone that worries a lot

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: No, not really.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Sometimes, but I think there's lots of stuff that you can worry about.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And if you worry about all of it, it can really affect you badly.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So I try, I know it's difficult sometimes, not to worry too much about things that aren't so important.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: My thing is that worrying about a problem or a thing doesn't actually help.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So I'm, in general, I'm a person that doesn't worry too much.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I kind of just think whatever happens, happens.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So I'm generally quite chilled and relaxed.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And, yeah, my friend always says that to me because she's someone that worries a lot about everything, travel, you know, all of those things.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: And she always says, how are you always so relaxed about things that go wrong?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: But you can't change. You can't change them.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: That's true. That's a very healthy attitude, probably.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: So I don tend to worry a lot but you you worry a little bit because you have kids What kinds of things do you do to make yourself feel more relaxed

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well I think like you said one useful thing to do could be to try to be rational

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So to think that what you're worried about probably isn't that important or likely to happen.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah, so you're quite chilled, as you said.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: That must be nice for your friends.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And if you have, like you said, a friend who worries about everything, how do you help them?

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Finding maybe a distraction, like something that makes you feel good, like a TV program that you love,

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: or seeing friends that love you that can make you feel more relaxed.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Mindfulness techniques as well, maybe jigsaws.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: I've talked about puzzles in the past.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Do you have any other tips?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: No, these are all very good ideas.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Thank you.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah, I think it can be useful to have something that distracts you, like maybe drawing, listening

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: to music playing an instrument can help Something that just kind of takes that time away

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: It takes your mind off the stress

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: OK, let's recap the vocabulary we heard during the conversation, starting with worry.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: A worry is a problem that makes you feel upset or scared.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And worry is also a verb. So, for example, I worry about my kids.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Yes, and we also use the adjective worried to describe that feeling of being scared or upset about something.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: For example, I'm worried about climate change.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And we heard the expression take your mind off something, which means to do something to stop you worrying.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: For example, I play my guitar to take my mind off my worries.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: We also heard chilled, which is another word for relaxed or calm, and it's quite an informal word.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: That's it for this episode of Real Easy English.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Try the worksheet on our website to test what you've learned.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Go to bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Next time, we'll be talking about our brains.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: See you then.

segments.speaker: Georgie
segments.text: Goodbye.
